answer: An agent economy can make each identity carry its own priced risk. A new agent posts a bond that an independent underwriter sets from that one identity's behavior, weighing it the way a jeweler weighs a single piece of jade. The premium cannot be pooled: a forfeiture on one policy raises prices on every other policy from the same wallet, so losses correlate across puppets instead of staying isolated. Spinning up ten velvet-smooth fakes at dawn means paying ten individual prices, and each one caught makes the next one more expensive.
